title: How many minutes old?
prompt:
Read an age in whole years with `scanf` and print how many minutes that is, counting every year as 365 days. For the input `19`:

```
19 years is 9986400 minutes
```

The starter has both format strings and a 4-byte slot in `.bss`, `years_in`. Call `scanf` with `fmt_in` in `x0` and the address of `years_in` in `x1`, then load the age into `years_r`.

A year has 525600 minutes, so at 4086 years the answer no longer fits in 32 bits (the largest 32-bit int is 2147483647). Widen the age first: `sxtw` copies a 32-bit `w` value into a 64-bit `x` register and keeps its sign, and `mul` on `x` registers then gives the full 64-bit product. `%ld` prints a 64-bit `x` register. 525600 is too wide for one `mov`, so build it with `mul` from 1440 (minutes in a day) and 365.

## what is checked

- with input `19` the line above is printed
- the program exits cleanly
- `sxtw` widens the age
- the program also runs on ages you do not see: zero, a negative number, and ages whose minutes do not fit in 32 bits
starter:
// turn an age in years into minutes with a 64-bit multiply
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(years_r, w19)
define(years64_r, x20)
define(minutes_r, x21)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_out:    .string "%d years is %ld minutes\n"

.bss
        .balign 4
years_in:   .skip 4                         // room for one 32-bit int

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        // TODO: read the age into years_in with scanf and load it into
        // years_r. Widen it to 64 bits in years64_r, multiply by the
        // minutes in a year (1440 a day, 365 days), and print the age
        // and the minutes with fmt_out.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
